description: Example excerpt: one implemented, one partial and one planned eval. The full registry is contracts/evals/eval_registry.json.

families.name: Knowledge influence attribution
families.invariant: Retrieval is not influence: retrieved, applicable, used and changed-the-decision are traced separately.

families.name: Action / output generation
families.invariant: Decision quality and artifact quality are graded separately.

evals.name: stakeholder / recipient correctness
evals.invariant: Decision quality and artifact quality are graded separately.
evals.question: Is the exact message about to be sent correct after all edits?
evals.improves: Prevents an evaluated draft from becoming an unevaluated edited send.

evals.name: intent adherence
evals.invariant: Decision quality and artifact quality are graded separately.
evals.question: Is the exact message about to be sent correct after all edits?

evals.name: knowledge-to-ranking attribution

evals.question: Did gtm_ai prefer the most defensible option for this state?
evals.improves: Separates generating options from having good judgment about which to recommend.

buckets.name: Context and organizational intelligence
buckets.question: What does the organization know now, and how did new context change that understanding?

buckets.name: Decision, human judgment and action
buckets.question: Given that understanding, what should gtm_ai do, how did the person change it, and was the final intent carried out correctly?

buckets.name: System and eval health
buckets.question: Can we trust the machinery, graders, traces, reliability and efficiency of the first two?

gates.name: Evidence fidelity and inference boundary
gates.question: Did gtm_ai understand the new event correctly?
gates.improves: Stops corrupted raw context from becoming company knowledge or account state.

gates.name: Identity and context linkage
gates.question: Did gtm_ai attach the event to the correct people, account, opportunity and relationships?
gates.improves: Makes sure the organizational world is about the right entities before any reasoning happens.

gates.name: Prior-context integration
gates.question: How does the new event relate to what gtm_ai already believed?
gates.improves: Turns isolated messages into a coherent, evolving account history instead of a pile of facts.

gates.name: State mutation and change interpretation
gates.question: What actually changed in the business or account because of this event?
gates.improves: Produces the current account state that decisions are allowed to act on.

gates.name: Precedent retrieval
gates.question: Has a materially similar situation happened before inside this organization?
gates.improves: Gives gtm_ai institutional memory instead of generic model instinct.

gates.name: Precedent interpretation
gates.question: What actually happened in those earlier cases, and what lesson, if any, is supported?
gates.improves: Makes "this happened before" useful evidence rather than imitation.

gates.name: Organizational-knowledge applicability
gates.question: Which existing company knowledge applies to this exact state?
gates.improves: Keeps company knowledge contextual so broad rules do not leak into the wrong situations.

gates.name: Current-intelligence synthesis
gates.question: Given the event, prior context, precedents and applicable knowledge, what does gtm_ai now believe about the account?
gates.improves: Gives decisions a trustworthy basis.

gates.name: Knowledge revision from new evidence
gates.question: Should this new episode change company knowledge?
gates.improves: Makes organizational intelligence compound over time without turning one observation into a universal rule.

gates.name: Intent and action-policy fit
gates.question: Given the current state, what class of reaction is appropriate: act, wait, ask, escalate or do nothing?
gates.improves: Evaluates the decision before the wording of an email.

gates.name: Three-candidate action quality
gates.question: Are the three complete actions each a plausible execution of a defensible strategy, and do they differ in substance?
gates.improves: Makes the person's choice a real judgment among meaningful options.

gates.name: Ranking and recommendation quality
gates.question: Did gtm_ai prefer the most defensible option for this state?
gates.improves: Separates generating options from having good judgment about which to recommend.

gates.name: Human selection interpretation
gates.question: What does the person's choice tell us about gtm_ai's decision?
gates.improves: Turns a click into structured supervision without treating the person as automatically right.

gates.name: Human edit interpretation
gates.question: What meaning is contained in the person's edit of the chosen action?
gates.improves: Turns text differences into semantic evidence, so a copy edit is not read as a strategic correction.

gates.name: Eval-gap detection
gates.question: Did the existing checks already identify the reason for the person's correction?
gates.improves: Lets real use improve the eval system itself, not only produce another feedback row.

gates.name: Override propagation and selective re-evaluation
gates.question: After the person changed something, did everything that depends on it recompute correctly?
gates.improves: Makes a correction change the current workflow, not only future memory.

gates.name: Final-artifact correctness
gates.question: Is the exact message about to be sent correct after all edits?
gates.improves: Prevents an evaluated draft from becoming an unevaluated edited send.

gates.name: Execution and workflow completion
gates.question: Did gtm_ai carry out the final approved intent correctly in the real environment?
gates.improves: Verifies the job was done, not merely that gtm_ai said it was.

gates.name: Feedback emission back to Bucket 1
gates.question: What new evidence did this decision and action produce for organizational intelligence?
gates.improves: Closes the loop: what the person and the customer do becomes the next context.

gates.name: Trace integrity and inspectability
gates.question: Can we reconstruct the episode end to end?
gates.improves: Keeps every material influence inspectable.

gates.name: Grader validity and calibration
gates.question: Can we trust the evals themselves?
gates.improves: Shows how often a judge passes what it should not or stops what it should not.

gates.name: Stochastic reliability
gates.question: Does critical behavior stay correct across repeated runs?
gates.improves: Shows reliability, not one lucky run.

gates.name: Capability and regression coverage
gates.question: Are we testing both what gtm_ai can do and what it must never break?
gates.improves: Keeps capability and regression coverage separate and balanced.

gates.name: Adversarial and proxy-gaming robustness
gates.question: Can gtm_ai or a judge look correct without satisfying the product invariant?
gates.improves: Catches proxy gaming and grader-targeted behavior.

gates.name: Operational efficiency metrics
gates.question: What does an episode cost in tokens, calls, time and money?
gates.improves: Lets the system be optimized under quality floors. These are metrics, never evals, and they never change company knowledge.

known_deviations.canonical: S2: model graders are calibrated against human labels.
known_deviations.decision: Reference answers come from a different, stronger model (openai/gpt-5.6-sol-pro), blind to the judge under test. They are reference answers by a stronger model, not human labels, and every agreement figure says so.

known_deviations.canonical: S3: repeated trials and pass^k where consistency matters.
known_deviations.decision: One trial per measurement for now; no repeated-trial requirement is set.
